conviction_note: The evidence leans slightly positive. Consensus of ~$4.93-4.98 sits about 7% below Q2's $5.32 and roughly at what the company's own guide implies. The September update moved fees to the high end of the range, and the 37bp NCO guide implies a doubling of H2 charge-offs that Q2 credit (23bp) and peer CRE trends do not yet show. Against that: MTB has sold 5 of its last 7 prints, the put skew is modestly positive, and peers' NII came in below their own guides. So p_up sits at 53 on an abs move of 3.5 (the thin-chain implied move of 5.46 is discounted toward the 2.37 median reaction but not to it), giving +0.21. The findings sum to +0.2 and agree with that.
bar: Q3 2026 adjusted EPS ~$4.93-4.98, revenue ~$2.53-2.54B. Sources: AAII/Zacks $4.93 from 15 analysts (https://www.aaii.com/investingideas/article/514993-what-you-need-to-know-about-mt-bank-corporations-q3-earnings, 2026-10-15); Earnings Whispers $4.98 consensus with a $5.12 whisper and $2.54B revenue (https://www.earningswhispers.com/stocks/MTB); iTiger $4.96 / $2.53B (https://www.itiger.com/news/1173450864, 2026-10-09). Company FY2026 guide, reiterated 2026-09-14: NII (TE) $7.2-7.35B in the bottom half, fees $2.8-2.85B at the high end, expense $5.5-5.6B at the high end, NCO ~37bp, tax ~24%, CET1 10.0-10.5% (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/36270/000003627026000052/mtb_3q26xinvestorpresent.htm). The guide arithmetic (H2 NII ~$1.84B a quarter, fees ~$705M, expense ~$1.40B, NCO-implied provision ~$165M, ~147.5M shares) gives ~$4.85-4.95, so consensus sits on the guide.
positioning_check: Short interest is about 5.3M shares, 3.7%, 4.4 days to cover (Equibles, ~2026-08-19, https://equibles.com/stocks/MTB). FINRA 2026-06-30 showed 6.0M shares and 4.54 days (CurvedTrading, per the sweep row). Not crowded. The 25d skew is +2.88 vol points (downside paid, modest). Put/call OI is 0.54, but total OI is only 279 and the ATM spread is 14% of mid, so the 5.46% event-implied move rests on a thin chain; ATM IV of 27.1% against 20d realised vol of 14%. The stock is -11.8% since the July 15 print against SPY +2.0% (AAII), -13.7% off its 52w high and -3.13% over 20d. The CEO's 10b5-1 sale filled at $239.35 on 2026-09-14, so roughly -8.5% of that fall came after the Sept 16 Fed hike and the 10y moving back above 5%.

findings.finding: M&T's 2026-09-14 investor update (8-K Ex 99.1) places FY2026 fee income at the HIGH END of $2.8-2.85B. On the 2026-07-15 call the CFO gave the range with no placement. The update reiterates NII in the bottom half and expense at the high end. With H1 fees at $1,429M ($689M + $740M), the high end implies ~$710M a quarter in H2, against consensus revenue of ~$2.53B that equals Q2's level.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q2 2026: fees $740M vs $689M (Bayview $47M, trust and swaps up) with a large EPS beat ($5.35 vs $4.66); the stock rose +2.76%, the only clearly positive reaction in the last 5 prints (baseline).
findings.why_not_priced: It is a public 8-K from a month ago, so mostly priced. The estimate trend shows little reaction: FY EPS estimates were -0.3% over the last month with 2 upward Q3 revisions and 0 down (AAII). If the market had fully priced it, revisions would be positive. What is left is that the Q3 print shows it in the reported line (sub-servicing +$35M in H2, any Bayview distribution).
findings.independence: The July call transcript gives the range without placement, which is the comparison for the move to 'high end' (https://www.mitrade.com/insights/news/live-news/article-8-1906021-20260716). Same company, different document.

findings.finding: The FY NCO guide of ~37bp (July call, reiterated 2026-09-14) against H1 actuals of $185M (Q1 $105M/31bp, Q2 $80M/23bp) implies H2 NCO of ~$165-175M a quarter, roughly double Q2. Q2 criticized CRE fell $990M in H1 to 10.1% of CRE (from 14.5%), and multifamily criticized fell to $160M of $7.1B. If Q3 charge-offs run nearer the H1 pace, provision lands $30-50M below a guide-built model, about +$0.15-0.25 of EPS against a $4.93-4.98 bar.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The last two prints with benign credit and a beat moved +2.76% (Q2 2026) and -1.55% (Q1 2026, a 2.7% beat). MTB has risen on 2 of its last 7 prints (baseline), so a credit-driven beat has not reliably paid.
findings.why_not_priced: Consensus at $4.93-4.98 is ~7% below Q2's $5.32 and close to guide-based arithmetic, which suggests models carry the 37bp NCO guide literally. MTB beat the last four quarters by an average of 8.95% (Zacks via search), and the whisper is $5.12. If the market had priced a benign-credit quarter, consensus would sit near the whisper.
findings.independence: Partly. WFC's Q3 2026 release (2026-10-13) shows CRE nonaccruals and the CRE allowance falling, though commercial NCO rose to 0.18% from 0.10% (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0000072971/000007297126000318/wfc3qer10-13x26ex991xrelea.htm). PNC's Q3 shows NPLs +8% driven by commercial, which points the other way (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0000713676/000162828026065936/q32026financialhighlightsa.htm).

findings.finding: Peer NII read-through is soft. PNC's Q3 2026 NII rose +2% q/q (NIM -2bp to 2.94%) against its own guided +3-3.5%, and fees fell 6% q/q. WFC's NII of ~$12.52B came in slightly below the ~$12.59B estimate. JPM raised its FY NII guide to ~$106.2B after the Sept 16 Fed hike. MTB guides NII to the bottom half of $7.2-7.35B and says it is neutral to short rates, so a JPM-style raise is unlikely and a PNC-style shortfall is the risk.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Not isolated for MTB. Q2 2026 NII rose 2% q/q to $1.804B TE (NIM flat at 3.70%) and the stock rose +2.76%. WFC traded -1.1% pre-market on its slight NII miss (finviz).
findings.why_not_priced: PNC released this morning and WFC two days ago, after MTB last spoke on Sept 14, so MTB consensus may not have absorbed a sector NII shortfall. Zacks has MTB NII at ~$1.81B, +2.5%. If priced, MTB would have underperformed peers today, and nothing seen shows that.
findings.independence: Proxy, not MTB's own number. Two independent peer documents (PNC 8-K; WFC via https://finviz.com/news/401783/wells-fargo-beats-third-quarter-profit-estimates-as-loan-growth-and-improved-efficiency-support-earnings). JPM points the other way (https://www.morningstar.com/stocks/jpmorgan-earnings-solid-results-despite-capital-markets-softening).

findings.finding: MTB is down 11.8% since its July 15 print against SPY +2.0% (AAII), and down ~8.5% from the $239.35 at which the CEO's 10b5-1 sale filled on Sept 14. Most of that came after the Sept 16 Fed hike to 3.75-4.00% and the 10y back above 5%. Management says it is neutral to short rates (July call), so the de-rating is macro and sector-wide rather than a company-specific bad number. That sets a low bar for a clean print and a reiterated guide.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q2 2026 came in after a weak run-in and rose +2.76% on a beat. Other prints with a negative 20d run-up are not separable in the baseline.
findings.why_not_priced: The drawdown is itself the market pricing the rate shock. The question is whether MTB's print reveals a rate cost the company does not have (it guides neutral to short rates). If the market saw MTB as rate-neutral, it would not have lagged SPY by ~14 points.
findings.independence: Fed hike and 10y >5%: https://investinglive.com/central-banks/fomc-rate-decision-fed-hikes-for-the-first-time-in-three-years/. The 'neutral on the short end' comment is from the July call (https://www.webull.com/news/15234169636742144).

findings.finding: NYC's Rent Guidelines Board froze stabilized rents at 0% for 1- and 2-year leases starting 2026-10-01. MTB's multifamily CRE book is $7.1B with only $160M criticized at 2026-06-30 (from $476M at year-end), so the direct credit effect inside this print is small, but analysts may ask about it on the call.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No MTB precedent. Multifamily upgrades drove the Q2 criticized decline, which the stock rewarded (+2.76%).
findings.why_not_priced: It is public since June and mostly priced. What remains is whether MTB discloses rent-regulated exposure or downgrades. If the market feared it, MTB would trade like NYC-multifamily lenders, and its criticized trend argues it does not.
findings.independence: MTB 10-Q multifamily criticized table (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0000036270/000003627026000050/mtb-20260630.htm) bounds the exposure.

findings.finding: An 8-K filed 2026-09-28 reclassifies the Q3 fee lines: debit interchange moves out of service charges into card revenues, trust and brokerage merge, and trading/derivative gains plus syndication move into capital markets. Loans held for sale are split from HFI. Total other income and EPS are unchanged. Zacks's service-charge consensus of $108.8M (-22.8% y/y) appears to reflect the reclass, so line-item 'misses' in headlines may be artefacts.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: None. This is the first quarter on the new presentation.
findings.why_not_priced: It is not a value item. It can only add headline noise to the first-minute reaction, in either direction.

findings.finding: Capital return is moderating. CET1 was 10.19% at Q2 (from 10.33%) against a stated ~10.2% target, and the CFO said buybacks are 'the tail on the dog', sized to RWA growth. Q2 buybacks were $465M against $1.25B in Q1. Guided strong CRE and consumer growth in Q3 consumes capital, so Q3 repurchases likely stay near or below the Q2 pace.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q2's buyback cut from $1.25B to $465M came with a +2.76% reaction, so the market looked through it then.
findings.why_not_priced: Mostly priced: the company said so in July. The residual is a Q3 number below the 12-month '8% of shares repurchased' run rate the September deck advertises.
findings.independence: Sept 2026 investor update, slide 6: 8% of shares repurchased over the last 12 months (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/36270/000003627026000052/mtb_3q26xinvestorpresent.htm). Same company.

baseline_tension: Mildly against the baseline. The evidence leans positive (beat pattern, fee guide at the high end, an NCO guide that looks conservative, a de-rated stock), while the skew is modestly put-bid (+2.88) and MTB has fallen on 5 of its last 7 prints. That keeps p_up at 53 rather than the 55-58 the fundamentals alone would suggest.
lessons_applied: Lesson 1: MTB has sold most beats (2 of 7 up), so the credit/beat finding was cut from +0.5 to +0.3 and print_vs_bar from 3.0 to 2.5.

Lesson 6: the fee 'high end' finding lands inside guidance the company already gave publicly, so it was cut from +0.4 to +0.2. The bar is sourced from four agreeing estimate sources plus the company guide, so no cap.

Lesson 5: the peer NII read is a proxy, so it was cut from -0.3 to -0.2. The positioning drawdown has a named macro cause (Fed hike, 10y >5%) but is still not company-level, so it was cut from +0.4 to +0.2.
Lesson 7: checked short interest (3.7%, 4.4 days, not crowded) before the negative findings, and kept p_up at 53, toward 50, because the positive lean runs against the put skew.
Unchanged: rent freeze -0.1, fee reclass 0.0, capital return -0.2.
